user.title: Welcome to Heating Assistant
user.description:
Heating Assistant uses model-predictive control to keep your home comfortable while minimising energy use. It learns your home's thermal behaviour and plans ahead using outdoor temperature and weather forecasts.

Start with the basics below. After setup you can add rooms, heat sources and schedules from the integration's **Configure** menu.

data_description.latitude: Decimal degrees, positive north of the equator. Used for solar gain prediction. Pre-filled from your Home Assistant location.
data_description.longitude: Decimal degrees, positive east of the prime meridian. Used for solar gain prediction. Pre-filled from your Home Assistant location.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: A local sensor measuring current outdoor temperature. At least one of this or the weather entity is required.
data_description.weather_entity: Provides hourly forecasts so the controller can plan ahead. At least one of this or the outdoor sensor is required.
data_description.update_interval: Re-planning cadence in seconds. 900 s (15 min) suits most homes; lower values respond faster but use more CPU.

global_settings.title: General & sensor settings
global_settings.description: Outdoor sources, pricing, and how often the controller re-plans.

data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: A local sensor measuring current outdoor temperature. Optional when a weather forecast entity is set.
data_description.weather_entity: Provides forecasts so the controller can plan ahead. Optional; if not set, an outdoor temperature sensor is required.
data_description.solar_radiation_entity: Optional. A sensor reporting the sun's solar irradiance (Global Horizontal Irradiance) in W/m² — e.g. Open-Meteo's shortwave_radiation, or a pyranometer — ideally with an hourly forecast in its attributes. When set, the forecast replaces the modelled clear-sky radiation in the solar-gain model (decomposed and transposed onto your windows by geometry); the clear-sky model stays as the automatic fallback. This is the sun's radiation, not solar-panel production.
data_description.price_entity: Optional. A sensor exposing hourly spot prices (Nord Pool, Tibber, Energi Data Service, etc.). When set, the controller accounts for electricity prices when planning heating.
data_description.price_net_tariff: Fixed grid / network tariff to add to the raw spot price, in the same currency per kWh as your price sensor (e.g. 0.20 DKK/kWh). Ensures the effective price seen by the controller is never below your actual cost of electricity.
data_description.price_spot_surcharge: Fixed spot price surcharge or electricity tax to add on top of the raw spot price, in the same currency per kWh as your price sensor (e.g. 0.90 DKK/kWh for Danish elafgift). Together with the net tariff this floors the effective price at a realistic consumer value.
data_description.update_interval: Re-planning cadence in seconds (60–3600). 900 s (15 min) suits most homes.

manage_rooms.title: Rooms, heaters & schedules
manage_rooms.description: Add rooms first. Each room can then have its own heaters, windows and time-of-day schedule.

add_room.title: Add a room
add_room.description: Tell Heating Assistant about a new room. The fields lower down (floor type, facade colour, thermal bridges, sky coupling) are optional refinements — leave them at the defaults if unsure.

data_description.name: A unique identifier for this room (e.g. 'Living Room'). Used as the climate entity name.
data_description.temp_sensors: Sensors measuring this room's indoor temperature. Pick one or more — multiple sensors are averaged.
data_description.window_sensors: Binary sensors that go ON when a window or door is open. The controller pauses heating when any of these are open.
data_description.room_size: Rough room volume. Determines the room's thermal mass; can be refined later from measured data.
data_description.building_age: Older buildings lose more heat. Determines the room's insulation level; refined automatically over time.
data_description.envelope_tightness: How draught-proof the envelope is. Affects how much heat is lost through wind-driven air infiltration.
data_description.comfort_offset: Symmetric band around the setpoint that's still considered comfortable. ±2 °C is typical.
data_description.floor_type: Advanced — underfloor heating and concrete slabs add a large slow thermal mass that the model can track separately.
data_description.facade_colour: Advanced — affects how much solar gain the opaque walls absorb. Darker = more absorption.
data_description.facade_solar_share: Advanced — fraction of window-derived solar gain attributed to the opaque facade (0 = ignored). Typical 0.2–0.6 when enabled.
data_description.thermal_bridge_psi_l: Advanced — extra heat loss from window frames, balcony slabs, etc. Leave at 0 if unknown — the model can infer it from data.
data_description.sky_radiative_ua: Advanced — long-wave radiation to the night sky (clear-night cooling). Leave at 0 if unknown.
data_description.solar_exposure: Quick alternative to listing individual windows: how much direct sun this room gets. Used only when no windows are added below; adding windows overrides it.
data_description.solar_facing: The direction the room's main glazing faces. Only used with the solar-exposure preset above.

manage_room_windows.title: Windows: pick a room
manage_room_windows.description: Choose which room's windows to configure.

remove_room.title: Remove a room
remove_room.description: This will delete the room and all of its heaters, windows and schedule periods. Cannot be undone.

manage_windows.title: Windows in {name}
manage_windows.description: Solar gain is computed for each configured window. Window-open detection uses the room's binary sensors instead.

add_window.title: Add a window to {name}
add_window.description: Tell Heating Assistant about a window so it can compute its solar gain.

data_description.area: The glazed surface area in m². Frames are not counted.
data_description.orientation: Compass direction the window faces (where the sun strikes it most directly).
data_description.tilt: Tilt of the window pane. 90° is a normal vertical window in a wall; 0° is a horizontal skylight.

remove_window.title: Remove a window from {name}
remove_window.description: Pick the window you want to delete.

manage_room_heaters.title: Heat sources: pick a room
manage_room_heaters.description: Choose which room's heat sources to configure.

manage_heaters.title: Heat sources in {name}
manage_heaters.description: Heaters are the actuators the controller drives. Each one is a Home Assistant switch entity.

add_heater.title: Add a heat source to {name}
add_heater.description: Configure a heater or heat pump. Performance details are optional and improve modelling accuracy.

data_description.name: Friendly name shown in the dashboard.
data_description.type: Electric heaters convert electricity 1:1 to heat. Heat pumps lift heat from outdoors at higher efficiency (COP > 1).
data_description.max_power: Rated thermal output in watts when fully on. For heat pumps this is the heat delivered, not the electrical input.
data_description.heater_entity: The Home Assistant switch that turns this heater on and off.
data_description.efficiency: Fraction of electrical input delivered as heat (0–1). Normally 1.0 for electric heaters.
data_description.cop_rated: Coefficient of performance at the reference outdoor temperature. Typical air-source heat pumps: 2.5–4.5.
data_description.cop_temp_ref: Outdoor temperature at which the rated COP applies. Manufacturer datasheets typically use 7 °C.
data_description.min_power: Lowest stable thermal output. 0 = no minimum. Helps the controller avoid short-cycling.
data_description.max_temp_offset: Largest temperature lift this heat pump will attempt at full power (°C above outdoor).
data_description.hvac_mode: Whether this unit can heat, cool, or do both.
data_description.emitter_time_constant: Lag between the controller's command and heat actually reaching the room. Radiators ≈ 600 s; fan coils ≈ 60 s; resistive heaters ≈ 0 s.

edit_heater.description: Pick which heat source to edit.

manage_room_schedule.title: Schedule: pick a room
manage_room_schedule.description: Choose which room's schedule to manage.

manage_schedule.title: Schedule for {name}
manage_schedule.description: Periods define time-of-day comfort and setback. Outside any active period the room uses its default setpoint.

add_period.title: Add a schedule period to {name}
add_period.description: Create a time-of-day setpoint override (e.g. warm in the evening, cool overnight). The bottom three fields are optional per-period tweaks.

data_description.name: A short label for this period (e.g. 'morning', 'night').
data_description.mode: Comfort = follow the setpoint. Off = disable heating (with frost protection).
data_description.start: Local time when this period begins.
data_description.end: Local time when this period ends. May cross midnight.
data_description.days: Leave empty to apply every day.
data_description.setpoint: Target temperature during this period. Leave at the room default if you don't want an override.
data_description.comfort_offset: Comfort band width during this period. Leave at the room default if you don't want an override.
data_description.tracking_weight: Advanced — multiplier on the global tracking strength during this period. 1.0 = no change.
data_description.energy_weight: Advanced — multiplier on the global energy penalty during this period. 1.0 = no change.
data_description.frost_protection: Minimum allowed temperature when this period is in 'off' mode.

edit_period.title: Edit period: {name}
edit_period.description: Update this period's timing and overrides.

simulate_thermal_response.name: Simulate thermal response
simulate_thermal_response.description: Run a standalone thermal simulation showing how a room responds to constant heating power.

room_name.name: Room name
room_name.description: Name of the room to simulate.

heating_power.name: Heating power
heating_power.description: Constant thermal power applied to the room (W).

set_schedule_enabled.name: Suspend or resume comfort schedule
set_schedule_enabled.description: Suspend or resume the comfort schedule for a room (or all rooms when none is specified). Useful for one-off exceptions to a sleep / setback schedule.

room_name.name: Room name
room_name.description: Optional room name. Leave blank to apply to all rooms.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: True to resume the schedule, false to suspend it.

estimate_parameters.name: Estimate thermal parameters
estimate_parameters.description: Back-calculate thermal_mass and r_external from an observed heating experiment.

heating_power.name: Heating power
heating_power.description: Constant thermal power applied during the experiment (W).

initial_temp.name: Initial temperature
initial_temp.description: Room temperature at the start of the experiment (°C).

final_temp.name: Final temperature
final_temp.description: Room temperature at the end of the experiment (°C).

regenerate_dashboard.name: Regenerate Lovelace dashboard
regenerate_dashboard.description: Build a complete per-room Lovelace dashboard from the current Heating Assistant configuration. Returns the YAML in the response and optionally writes it to <config>/dashboards/.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Return YAML only, do not write a file or create a notification.

filename.name: Output filename
filename.description: Plain filename (no path) inside <config>/dashboards. Defaults to heating_assistant.yaml.

compute_loglik_slice.name: Compute log-likelihood slice
compute_loglik_slice.description: Evaluate the CD-EKF PED log-likelihood on a (log C, log R_ext) grid centred on the room's current MLE. Drives the Diagnostics dashboard's likelihood-landscape card.

room_name.name: Room name
room_name.description: Room whose parameters should be sliced.

n_grid.name: Grid points
n_grid.description: Number of grid points per axis (odd preferred).

span_log.name: Half-width (log)
span_log.description: Half-width of the slice in log-units. 1.0 ≈ factor 2.7.
